title: Crumpling, Hugging, Skipping, Switching Off & Letting Go
description: Paper that creases under your finger, bubbles that hug their wrap, underlines that skip gaps, inert subtrees, self-closing dialogs.

drops.title: Crumple & Release
drops.description: Drag across a sheet to paint crumple into its mesh; tap to ball it up or flatten it out again.
drops.concept: The Codrops original bakes a Vellum cloth simulation in Houdini and replays it in Three.js through vertex animation textures. This rebuild keeps the feel and drops the pipeline: a creased height field made of sharpened fold planes, a per-vertex crumple amount you paint with the pointer, and flat shading recomputed from the deformed normals every frame in canvas 2D.
drops.source: Toi Nagasawa — 'Building an Interactive Crumpled Paper Effect with Houdini VAT and Three.js' on Codrops

interaction.mouse: Drag over a sheet to crease it locally; sliders move the light, crease scale and fold depth
interaction.click: A tap without dragging balls the whole sheet up, or flattens it if it is already crumpled
interaction.touch: Same drag-to-crumple with touch; the rig panel is hidden on narrow screens

drops.title: Shrink-Wrapped Bubbles
drops.description: A chat bubble sized to the shape its text actually wrapped to, not to the width it was allowed to use.
drops.concept: A block box is as wide as its widest permitted line, so balanced text leaves dead space on the right. Naming the inline text with anchor-name lets a pseudo-element background take anchor-size() instead. The demo audits its own engine: where anchor-size() hands back the whole inline box rather than the word fragments, it measures the same geometry from the fragments and says so on the badge.

interaction.mouse: Drag the column slider to rewrap the thread; switch between text-wrap modes
interaction.click: Toggle between the shrink-wrapped bubble and the plain block box, or force the measured box
interaction.touch: The column breathes on its own until you touch it, then the controls take over

drops.title: Underlines That Skip the Gaps
drops.description: One continuous rule becomes a stroke per word — editorial underline, marker pass and changelog strike.
drops.concept: text-decoration-skip-spaces landed in the Chrome 155 beta: all cuts the decoration at every space, while start and end trim only the edges. Three specimens toggle between none and all, with thickness and offset on sliders. Where the property is missing, the page rebuilds each line as per-word inline boxes and decorates those instead, so the comparison still reads.

interaction.mouse: Sliders set decoration thickness and underline offset
interaction.click: Switch between skip-spaces: none and all — the page alternates on its own until you do
interaction.touch: Buttons are full-size on mobile; the rig panel hides below 900px

drops.title: Switched Off, Still There
drops.description: A dimmed card that keeps its place but takes no focus, no clicks and no place in the accessibility tree.
drops.concept: interactivity: inert applies the inert flag from a stylesheet instead of an attribute, which suits paginated UI where only one step should be live. Tab through the deck and focus never leaves the active card; click a dimmed one and the hit is counted as ignored with a ripple where it landed. Engines without the property get the inert attribute and the badge says which path is running.

interaction.mouse: Click a step to make it the live one, or turn inert off to compare
interaction.click: Clicks on dimmed cards bounce and are tallied as ignored
interaction.touch: Tap to switch steps; the focus log reads back whatever last took focus

drops.title: Dialogs That Decide How They Close
drops.description: Light dismiss, Esc-only and deliberate-exit modals from one attribute instead of an outside-click listener.
drops.concept: closedby="any" closes on an outside click or Esc, closerequest keeps Esc but ignores the scrim, and none waits for your own control. Each dialog animates in and out with @starting-style and allow-discrete transitions on both the box and its ::backdrop, and a log reports what closed the last one. Without the attribute the same semantics are scripted, and the badge says so.
drops.source: 2026 write-up on native dialog light dismiss and the closedby attribute

interaction.mouse: Open each modal and try the scrim; only the any variant gives way
interaction.click: In-dialog buttons always close; the log names the gesture that did it
interaction.touch: Tap outside or use the close button; the none variant shakes when refused
